title: Cosmos
description: Everything that is: the world, the heavens above it and the endless void of stars enveloping both, as well as the astral spaces that lie parallel to them.
summary: Everything that is: the world, the heavens, the void of stars, and the astral spaces beside them.

title: The Outer Spheres
description: A layered astral plane beyond the waking world, reached by projecting the mind out of the body. It has no ground, gravity or physics, only endless distance filled with swirling stars and drifting lights, and it grows stranger and less ordered the further out one goes. Here and there, vast structures of no earthly making float in the void.
summary: A layered astral plane reached by projecting the mind, growing stranger and less ordered the further out one goes.

title: Known World
description: A vast and varied land of distinct nations and uneasy alliances, from the terraced island empire of Haenara in the far east to the ruins of Ostvengr in the north. Civilization asserts itself through commerce and conquest: the Levantine Vizierate holds the trade of the east, Great Forks taxes what passes between, and a kingdom stands at the centre of it all. On that kingdom's rugged coastline, a neglected Ancestral Estate sits apart from these machinations, harboring secrets that will soon draw eyes away from the concerns of the wider world.
summary: A vast land of nations from Haenara to fallen Ostvengr, functioning through trade and war while ancient secrets linger in the margins.

title: Loess
description: A broad plain of windblown yellow soil southwest of the Kingdom, fertile and easy to farm, and crowded with small kingdoms, duchies and city-states. The Kingdom conquered it long ago and lost it piece by piece over centuries as the crown weakened. Its courts speak Common and keep much of the Kingdom's ways, but none will kneel to it again, and they fight the Kingdom and one another for supremacy.
summary: A fertile western plain of small rival kingdoms, once the Kingdom's conquest and now its splinters.

title: Gilneas
description: The ruins of a small kingdom on the Loess plain, its walls built wide enough to enclose fields and orchards as well as the town, so that it could feed itself through a long siege. Inside them stand the shells of foundries and gunsmiths' works, cold now, with the river docks silted up and the fields gone back to grass. The walls were breached in the end, and the people who outlived the siege carry a wolf-curse, the last desperate resort of their former king. A few of them still live among the ruins.
summary: The walled ruins of a gunsmith kingdom on the Loess plain, whose surviving people carry their king's wolf-curse.

title: Amurgia
description: A hill town of Loess beneath a sheer bluff, its face honeycombed with hollows where bats roost by the thousand. Halfway up the bluff sits a small walled hamlet, overlooked by a castle at the top. Across a deep ravine stands a tall tower on its own pillar of earth, once joined to the castle by a stone bridge, and on some nights a light burns in its window. The princely house that rules Amurgia now keeps its court in the town below, where the shutters close at dusk as the bats pour out of the bluff.
summary: A Loess hill town beneath an old castle and a cut-off tower, where the shutters close at dusk as the bats come out.

title: Great Forks
description: A city-state where three rivers meet, holding the trade between the Kingdom and the Vizierate and taxing all of it. Its fields and orchards run for a day's ride in every direction and feed a population far larger than they should, the difference made up by barge. Great Forks has no state faith and suppresses none, which has made it a refuge for creeds beaten out of everywhere else, and a byword elsewhere for laxity.
summary: A wealthy river city-state on the trade road between the Kingdom and the Vizierate, which tolerates every faith and enforces none.

title: The Thousand Temples
description: The heart of the city, where every faith that ever came upriver built a house and few have been pulled down since. Shrines stand shoulder to shoulder along the water, grand ones with priesthoods and painted domes beside single rooms with one attendant and a locked door. The festival calendar runs past three hundred days a year and several fall together, so the noise rarely stops; children of the quarter learn early which processions pay best to join.
summary: The temple quarter of Great Forks, packed with shrines of every faith and in festival most days of the year.

title: The Levantine Vizierate
description: The great power of the east, a belt of desert and river-cities that an unknown conqueror welded together from sultanates, republics and free cities centuries ago, promising autonomy to those who joined and destruction to those who resisted. Its people are prosperous and well educated, its careful, licensed sorcery has advanced both its medicine and its warfare, and its soldiery, in teal and silver, is drilled rather than raised. Mountain passes guard it from the west, where it has fought Ostvengr and others for generations. The Vizier has ruled it since he took the throne from the foreign king who held it, and has not aged since; his made Janissaries do not age either, and no one has tested him twice. Those who stay beneath his notice live well.
summary: The rich and orderly Vizierate of the east, ruled for centuries by an unaging usurper who took the throne by murder.

title: Ostvengr
description: Until recently the strongest nation in the world, warmongering yet impenetrable behind their mountains, yet now a wasteland its neighbours are walling off rather than dividing. Ostvengr's advantage was never invention: its expeditions brought something back from underground, the Maw of Darkness, and its engineers spent generations building it into everything from field guns to kitchen appliances, over written warnings they overruled. It turned on them in a single day, an event known as the Fall. What is left is factory country full of machines that are still moving, a scatter of survivors who each blame a different part of it, and a border of river and mountain held by other people's armies. Nobody knows what became of the Kaiserin or her daughter.
summary: A fallen industrial empire, undone in a day by the eldritch machinery it built its supremacy on.

title: The Maw of Darkness
description: A shaft in the mountains that Ostvengr found and did not stop descending. Material and knowledge came up out of it, barely comprehensible and enormously useful, and the empire built everything it had on what it took from the shaft. The first expeditions went down unprotected, and the men who came back from those were not entirely the men who went down; every expedition after that went in sealed machines. Nobody has gone in since the Fall, and nobody can say whether the corruption that took the country came up the shaft or was already in what had been carried out of it.
summary: The shaft beneath Ostvengr's mountains that its expeditions descended, and the source of everything the empire became.

title: The Valley
description: A hot, sunken expanse of dunes and buried ruin at the northern edge of the Vizierate's reach, held by nobody and claimed by several. The Kvarotz built an empire here and vanished from it without explanation, leaving necropolises under the sand, vaults nobody has emptied, and machines that still run on something worse than fuel. Three tribes of Wildlanders hold the surface in confederation, the Vizier's expeditionary force is dug into the tombs and has not advanced in a long while, and everything the Kvarotz made of their slaves is still down in the mines. What draws all of them is amber: raw it sickens and ruins, refined it makes weapons and gear nothing else can match.
summary: A contested desert frontier of Kvarotz ruins and amber, fought over by Wildlander tribes and a stalled Levantine expedition.

title: The Northern Forest
description: An old forest in the cold north, beyond any border worth defending, where the beasts run larger than they have any business being. The Wildlanders send their young there to be marked: find the animal your god wears, survive it, and come home with the scar to prove it. Most of the pilgrims are girls, and most of the ones who do not return were boys. Nobody lives there. The tribes that use it are scattered across half the world and have not shared a homeland in generations, so the forest is the only ground all of them still hold in common.
summary: A cold northern forest of oversized beasts, where Wildlanders go to be scarred by their gods' animals and come back warriors.

title: Chernozem
description: A cold northern country organised entirely around a war it has been fighting since before it had records of anything else. It has good soil and a great many people, and no other industry worth the name. The army takes what it needs of both, and nobody argues. Now that the enemy has destroyed itself the country is quieter than it has been in living memory, and its officers are looking for the next war rather than waiting for one.
summary: A cold northern war-state that fought Ostvengr for its whole recorded history, and is already looking for its next war.

title: The Black Earth
description: The strip of ground between Chernozem and Ostvengr's mountains, and the only ground the two could ever fight over, since everything east of it is impassable. Generations of offensives have crossed it in both directions and neither side has held it for long. The soil is dark and enormously fertile, and nobody farms it. Chernozem took its name from this place rather than the other way round.
summary: The dark fertile frontier between Chernozem and Ostvengr, fought over for generations and farmed by nobody.

title: Podzola
description: Chernozem's northern half, named for its pale ash-grey soil. Winters are long and harsh, it grows little worth taking and, far from Chernozem's eternal war, it has been mostly ignored. The old songs are still sung here and the old rites still observed, and sects the Light's churches believe stamped out meet in cellars.
summary: Chernozem's poor-soiled northern half, too worthless to fight over, where old songs and older heresies survived the war years intact.

title: The Far North
description: Podzola past the last of its forts, where the farms end and the country stops pretending to be governed. A few settlements sit on the rivers and the rest of the people follow the reindeer, paying their tribute in furs to a capital none of them has seen and otherwise going years without meeting anyone who could name them. The church reached this far only thinly, too weak to root out the old animist faiths or the sects that hide among them. The garrisons collect what they are owed and do not ask what is further north.
summary: The frontier beyond Podzola's forts, where herders pay tribute in furs and the church holds too thinly to root out the old animist faiths.

title: Winterhome
description: The land past the last of the reindeer herders, where the winter does not break and never has. Nothing is farmed here and nobody lives here except hardened wildlife, winter demons, and the sorcerer Koschei. What is known of it comes from the old epics, which are songs about heroes who went north and are not reliable about anything else.
summary: The land beyond the reindeer herders, where the winter never breaks and nothing lives but the winter demons and Koschei.

title: Craie
description: A country of pale downland and chalk hills west of Ostvengr's mountains, wealthy in wine and wheat and nothing else, which spent two generations as the ground its neighbour's wars were fought across. Its nobility still prides itself on the finest fencing academies and duelling salons in the world, though the trenches taught its army to fight with artillery and spades rather than blades, and the academies have been slowly losing patrons and students since. Its army is large, conscripted, and mostly made of farmers who learned to live in cellars. Now that Ostvengr has destroyed itself, Craie is left with an intact army, no enemy, and fencing masters who have begun looking abroad for students and patrons.
summary: A chalk-hilled downland country west of Ostvengr, whose proud duelling traditions have been slowly losing ground to two generations of trench warfare.

title: Elurmendi
description: High mountains along Craie's frontier with Ostvengr, snowbound half the year and crossed by a few high passes where avalanches close the roads without warning. Its herders live under Craie's crown but are not of its people, keeping their own tongue and an old local faith whose monastic orders shelter travellers on the passes and keep to silence higher up. Since Ostvengr's fall, the passes lead only to a closed border, and masterless soldiers have come up from the lowlands looking for plunder.
summary: Snowbound frontier mountains under Craie's crown, home to a herding people with their own tongue and faith.

title: The Aterpe
description: A stone hospice at the top of a high pass, kept by a brotherhood that shelters travellers and digs the lost out of the snow with great shaggy mountain dogs. Its infirmary treats frostbite and fever with herbs, minerals and the old remedies of the mountain shepherds. Masterless soldiers burned it after Ostvengr's fall, and the brothers are rebuilding it with their own hands, new timber rising on the blackened walls.
summary: A hospice on a high pass whose brothers and great dogs dig travellers out of the snow, rebuilding since soldiers burned it.

title: Goiko Santutegia
description: A monastery of dark stone high above the passes, where an order of ascetics lives in near-silence and has little to do with the world below. Its brothers keep a hard rule of fixed hours: up before dawn, prostrations through the day, no food after dark. They hunt the peaks' wolves for their pelts, and mark themselves in blue ink as their years of discipline accumulate. Most who climb to it come to answer for something, and few come down again.
summary: A silent monastery high in the peaks, whose wolf-pelted, tattooed brothers keep a hard rule, and where men go to answer for something.

title: Juste Mesure
description: L'Académie de la Juste Mesure, one of Craie's old schools of the sword, its long hall marked out in chalked pistes and hung with the colours of its masters. The war thinned its patrons and students, but several dozen still train under a handful of masters, each of whom chooses an heir to carry their forms. The master called the Dragon was killed on its floor in a sanctioned bout, and with his chosen heir sent away, the rival who killed him, now known as le Pourfendeur, is unquestionably the school's finest blade.
summary: One of Craie's last great fencing academies, a long hall of chalked pistes hung with the colours of its masters.

title: La Compagnie de Salubrité
description: The guildhouse of the Compagnie de Salubrité, which has fought disease and infestation for generations, standing on the quays of a Craien river port. Its offices sort the letters that bring it contracts from across the world, and its archive holds generations of outbreaks charted street by street. Its men go out in yellow coats, and in Craie a town knows what their arrival means. On an island in the river stands the Company's lazaretto, where the sick and the suspected wait out their quarantine.
summary: The riverside guildhouse of Craie's yellow-coated sanitation company, with its own quarantine island in the river.

title: Université de Craie
description: Craie's great university, whose faculty of medicine is the most renowned in the world and draws students from every country that can afford to send them. It keeps anatomy theatres, a physic garden of medicinal plants and chairs in pharmacology, and is one of the few universities anywhere to let bird-folk hold them. Craie's army was never the strongest in the war, but the university's surgeons and physicians kept more of it alive than any other.
summary: Craie's great university, the world's leading school of medicine, and one of the few where bird-folk hold chairs.
